title: Lab 1 Report
text: In this lab, the E155 development board was assembled and tested to confirm the NUCLEO-32 MCU and UPduino v3.1 FPGA functionality. A design was implemented on the FPGA to control an on-board LED with the on-board high-speed oscillator, as well as control two additional on-board LEDs and an external 7-segment display using combinational logic of switch inputs.

title: E155 Portfolio
text:
Natalie Ko is an Engineering Major at Harvey Mudd College with a Science, Technology, and Society concentration. She’s interested in mechatronics and robotics. On campus, she works as a Repair Steward for Harvey Mudd’s Makerspace, CAD Lab TA/Grutor/Designer for the E4 course, and Shop Proctor for the Machine Shop.
When Natalie isn’t working on coursework or on-campus jobs, she works on other cool Engineering personal projects, including iterating on functional Spiderman web-shooters since 2018. She’s primarily drawn to projects that help foster a more accessible world.
